neighbours.label: importance adjectives as predicates before 'in' ('was instrumental / crucial / indispensable in')
fire: Her research was instrumental in securing funding for the new hospital.
Local volunteers were crucial in rebuilding the school after the flood.
The coach has been instrumental in developing young players at the club.
Satellite data proved indispensable in tracking the spread of the fire.
His testimony was critical in convincing the jury of her innocence.
The foundation will be instrumental in supporting rural health clinics.
Community leaders were pivotal in negotiating the ceasefire last year.
Early detection is vital in preventing the disease from spreading.
quiet: Her research was published in a journal about public hospitals.
Local volunteers were present in the school after the flood.
The coach has been working in the youth academy at the club.
Satellite data was stored in a database about the spread of the fire.
His testimony was recorded in the minutes of the hearing.
The foundation will be based in a small town near the clinics.
Community leaders were seated in the front row during the ceremony.
Early detection is common in countries with screening programmes.
